subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted API vs current provider
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finlytics.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@finlytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted API vs current provider

Hi Sam / Priya \u0014

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the SLOs and what we need to validate for Hosted API vs your current provider.

Summary from our call:
- Current provider (your measurements): end-to-end p95 ~480ms, p99 ~900ms (across your typical 512-token prompts).
- FinLytics target for production: end-to-end p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 800ms.
- Throughput needs: sustained baseline ~50 RPS, concurrency up to ~200 concurrent requests during peak windows; short spikes up to ~600 RPS for <60s.
- Streaming: you rely on token-by-token partial deliveries for the UI; partial-response latency (time-to-first-byte) target: <120ms p95.

What we need from your side to validate:
1) Sample traces/timings for a representative workload (attached is a small tracer format we can ingest). Please include both usual traffic and spike samples.
2) Typical request size distribution (tokens in / tokens out) and percentage of streaming sessions.
3) Any upstream network constraints (e.g., if you terminate TLS upstream, use of regional CDNs) that could affect end-to-end numbers.

What we’ll do on our side:
- Run side-by-side perf runs against our Hosted API and a comparable config on your current provider using your traces. We’ll measure end-to-end p95/p99, time-to-first-byte for streaming, and tail behavior during bursts.
- Share a short write-up and a latency comparison PDF with methodology and raw numbers.

Attached: request template for traces (finlytics_trace_samples_20270429.json) \u0014 if you can send a populated example that would speed the analysis.

Next steps / proposed timeline:
- Sam / Priya: send traces + distribution by EOD Monday (5/3).
- We'll schedule a 30m tech deep-dive the week of 5/3 to go over trace details and test plan.
- Deliver initial latency comparison by 5/7.

Thanks \u0014 happy to coordinate times.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
redwood.ai

[Attachment: finlytics_trace_samples_20270429.json]

From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finlytics.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted API vs current provider

Hi Laura / Marissa \u0014

Thanks for the recap. Per your request I’m attaching a small sample set of traces and a CSV with our request-size distribution. Quick clarifications inline:

- Our current measured numbers are indeed around p95 480ms, p99 900ms on our provider (these are end-to-end, browser -> app -> provider -> model -> app -> browser).
- Targeting p95 <= 400ms and p99 <= 800ms is what product is asking for.
- Throughput: base 50 RPS, sustained window 200 RPS, spikes measured historically up to 600 RPS for 30\u001390s.
- Streaming: ~35% of sessions use streaming; time-to-first-byte measured at p95 ~180ms today (so we need improvement there).

Attached: finlytics_trace_samples_20270429.json (contains 120 sample request traces) and request_distribution_20270429.csv. Note the traces include client-side queuing and CDN hops. If you want raw server-side logs only we can provide those as well.

Let us know what format you prefer for the perf runs and whether you need test tokens / a staging account to reproduce exactly.

Sam
Head of Infrastructure, FinLytics
sam.torres@finlytics.com

[Attachment: finlytics_trace_samples_20270429.json]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@finlytics.com>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@finlytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted API vs current provider

Hi Sam / Priya \u0014

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the traces. I skimmed the samples \u0014 good variety. Proposed next steps from our infra/perf side:

1) Dylan (cc’d) will run an initial ingest of your traces against our Hosted API in a staging project. We will run both single-request (non-streaming) and streaming profiles to capture time-to-first-byte.
2) We'll replay spikes to emulate the 600 RPS short bursts and capture p95/p99 tail behavior under your concurrency patterns.
3) We'll also run a comparable test against a config matched to your current provider (same model size, batching and quantization knobs where possible) to provide apples-to-apples numbers.

Deliverables:
- Latency comparison PDF (attached): methodology, p50/p95/p99 numbers, TTFB for streaming, summary of any observed jitter or queuing.
- Raw result CSVs and a short notes doc describing staging config and any config differences.

Practical asks for the tech run:
- Can you provide a short-lived API key or a test tenant for reproducing exactly? If not, we can stub the client-side delays but it’s best to have end-to-end.
- Are there any IP allowlists or VPN endpoints we should expect to configure?

Proposed scheduling: 30m tech sync on Wed 5/5 at 10:00 PT. If that works for you we’ll send a calendar invite.

I’ve attached a short latency comparison we typically use as a template \u0014 it will be filled with your numbers after the runs.

-Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: redwood_p95_p99_latency_comparison_20270430.pdf]

From: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@finlytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finlytics.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO: p95/p99 end-to-end latency - hosted API vs current provider

Hi Marissa / Laura \u0014

That timing works for us. We can provision a short-lived test API key and open IP access to Redwood’s staging CIDR \u0014 I’ll ask our infra team to get that done by EOD Tuesday (5/4).

A couple notes that might help the tests:
- Please run both browser-side end-to-end replays (to include CDN & client queuing) and server-side-only (to isolate provider/model latency).
- For streaming, prioritize time-to-first-byte and percent-of-frames-delivered within 200ms.

I’ll accept the invite for Wed 5/5 10:00 PT once you send it. Looking forward to the results.

Thanks,
Priya Reddy
Head of Product, FinLytics
priya.reddy@finlytics.com
